title: "Shared Socioeconomic Pathways"
subtitle: "SSP scenario data used as socioeconomic covariates in the SEA Provinces model and as future projection context for the Taiwan BSA model"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import pathlib
import pandas as pd

ssp_dir = pathlib.Path("../climate-projection-module/data/processed/SSP")
```

Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) are a set of five global scenarios describing plausible futures for
societal development through 2100 (SSP1–SSP5). They were developed by the climate research community
alongside the IPCC AR6 process and are widely used to contextualise climate impact projections. In this study:

- **Arm 1 (SEA Provinces):** Population projections from SSP1, SSP2, and SSP3 scenarios are used directly
  as node-level covariates in the STGNN, capturing how demographic change modulates dengue transmission
  dynamics across provinces.
- **Arm 2 (Taiwan BSA):** SSP population and urbanisation trajectories provide future projection context
  for evaluating dengue risk under different development pathways, combined with TCCIP regional climate
  projections.

---

## Arm 1 — Southeast Asia Provinces

### SSP Population Projections by Province

Population projections at admin-1 level under SSP1 (sustainability), SSP2 (middle of the road), and
SSP3 (regional rivalry) scenarios, derived from the CMIP6-aligned SSP database.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-ssp-sea-population
#| fig-cap: "SSP population projections for SEA admin-1 provinces, 2010–2100, under SSP1, SSP2, and SSP3."

import plotly.graph_objects as go

ssp_sea_path = ssp_dir / "sea_admin1_population.tsv"

if not ssp_sea_path.exists():
    print("⚠️  SEA SSP population data not found — run climate-projection-module/scripts/extract_ssp_population.py first.")
else:
    df = pd.read_csv(ssp_sea_path, sep="\t")
    fig = go.Figure()
    for scenario in df["scenario"].unique():
        subset = df[df["scenario"] == scenario]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=subset["year"], y=subset["population_mean"],
            mode="lines", name=scenario,
        ))
    fig.update_layout(
        title="Mean Admin-1 Population by SSP Scenario — SEA",
        xaxis_title="Year", yaxis_title="Population",
        legend_title="SSP Scenario", height=400,
    )
    fig.show()
```

### SSP Urbanisation Rate by Province

Urban fraction of population is a key driver of dengue vector density. SSP2 and SSP3 diverge substantially
in projected urbanisation rates across SEA countries.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-ssp-sea-urban
#| fig-cap: "Placeholder: SSP urbanisation rate projections for SEA admin-1 provinces."

ssp_urban_path = ssp_dir / "sea_admin1_urbanisation.tsv"
if not ssp_urban_path.exists():
    print("⚠️  SEA SSP urbanisation data not found — run climate-projection-module/scripts/extract_ssp_urbanisation.py first.")
else:
    df = pd.read_csv(ssp_urban_path, sep="\t")
    print(df.head())
```

### SSP Feature Contribution to STGNN

The table below summarises how SSP variables are incorporated into the SEA STGNN feature set.

| SSP Variable | Scenario(s) Used | Role in Model |
|---|---|---|
| Population (total) | SSP2 (baseline) | Node feature — scales absolute case counts |
| Population density | SSP2 | Node feature — proxy for human-vector contact rate |
| Urban fraction | SSP1, SSP2, SSP3 | Node feature — affects vector habitat availability |
| GDP per capita | SSP2 | Node feature — proxy for healthcare access / reporting capacity |

### Ageing Population and Dengue Vulnerability (Taiwan)

Taiwan's rapidly ageing population is an important modulator of dengue severity. Older adults face higher
hospitalisation and case fatality rates. SSP projections indicate Taiwan's median age rising significantly
through 2050, which will be incorporated as a BSA-level demographic covariate.

---

> **Note on scenario selection:** The SEA STGNN is trained and validated under historical conditions (2011–2018)
> and uses SSP2 population data as the primary covariate. SSP1 and SSP3 are included as sensitivity
> scenarios for prospective risk projections only. For operational monthly inference, SSP2-4.5 is used
> throughout for consistency with the AR6 climate delta correction.
